corrections: OVERHANG MECHANISM IS STALE, NOT LIVE: the bear's central claim that 'every few months another ~$1B block is dumped, mechanically capping the price' fails against primaries. The last BC Partners marketed block priced June 23, 2025 (23,952,096 Class A shares at $41.95, ~$1.005B, with a concurrent $100M company repurchase) - over 12 months ago. The Class B count is frozen at 176,478,229 from the Feb 1, 2026 10-K through the May 3, 2026 10-Q through the May 2026 proxy record date, and EDGAR shows no subsequent selling-stockholder prospectus. The stock fell from ~$43.5 to ~$20.6 WITHOUT any BC supply, so the current cheapness is a fundamental repricing (see next item), not the technical the debate attributes it to.

THE DERATING DRIVER THE DEBATE MISSED: the June 10, 2026 Q1 print beat, but management CUT FY2026 net-sales guidance to $13.40-13.55B (+6.3-7.5%) and guided active-customer adds to the LOW end of the 150-250K/quarter range, citing a softer consumer; the stock fell ~11% over the following five sessions. The bear's 'slow-growth mature retailer' leg is verified and strengthened; the 'valley of death is supply of stock, not demand' framing is wrong on current evidence.

'NO DATED EVENT / NO GOVERNANCE RESET / CHEAPNESS CAN PERSIST INDEFINITELY' IS OVERSTATED: the court-filed settlement in the Gilbert v. BC Partners derivative suit (8-K Ex 99.1/99.2, April 2026; hearing June 23, 2026) recites that the October 2023 Downstream Merger included governance changes 'including a five-year sunset of Chewy's Class B Common Stock' (super-voting rights end ~2028) plus BC tax indemnities, and the suit itself settled for $29.5M paid TO Chewy. Dual-class entrenchment has a documented contractual end-date; treat the exact trigger date as recital-verified only, but 'no governance reset on the table' is false as stated.

NET-INCOME-DECLINE CAUSALITY IS A TAX ARTIFACT: FY25 NI $222.8M vs FY24 $392.7M (-43%) verifies as a number, but FY24 included a $241.0M income-tax BENEFIT while FY25 carried a $40.5M provision; pre-tax income GREW +74% ($151.7M to $263.3M) and the latest quarter's NI is UP 52% YoY ($94.8M vs $62.4M, 2.8% net margin). 'Heavy stock-comp eats real profit' fails as the causal story (TTM SBC ~1.7% of revenue, roughly flat). The bear's 'ROIC ~3.9%' does not verify on current financials - FY25 EBIT $267.9M against invested capital of roughly $0.7-1.3B implies mid-teens-plus returns (FMP TTM ROIC ~20%); the 3.9% is a stale screener artifact.

NET-CASH FRAMING SUPERSEDED POST-QUARTER: the ~$36M net cash verified as of May 3, 2026 (cash+investments $520.1M vs $484.1M operating-lease liabilities, zero borrowings, per 10-Q), but on June 23, 2026 Chewy entered a NEW $600M seven-year senior secured term loan (JPMorgan agent, SOFR+1.75%, ~1%/yr amortization, first/second-priority lien on substantially all assets) and extended the ABL to June 23, 2031. Chewy is no longer a debt-free story; leverage is modest (~0.8x FY25 adj EBITDA) and likely funds buybacks, but secured debt now sits above the equity.

MINOR NUMBER FIXES: BC Partners economic stake is 43.2% (88.4% voting) at the May 2026 proxy record date, not 'toward 47%' - the sell-down is further along than the bear states; TTM gross profit is ~$3.79B, not ~$4.0B (SoP gross-profit anchors ~5% overstated); share count ~409-410M verifies (232.5M A + 176.5M B); TTM FCF $584M verifies (FMP TTM FCFE $583.8M, EV/FCF ~14.6x at $20.60); insider zero-open-market-buys verifies (Form 4 statistics: totalPurchases=0 every quarter 2024Q1-2026Q2), though the '~44M shares sold' is dominated by BC block dispositions, not management dumping. Risk/reward at the current $20.60 (vs the $19.6 anchor) compresses to roughly 1.1:1 ($15 downside / $27 base), below the stated 1.6:1.
